newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil edge down on crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil edge down on crude.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps edged down marginally at midday on Thursday on weaker overnight crude values in lacklustre trade with the market seen looking for fresh direction, traders said.
"The market is drifting right now, there is no clear direction. Alot depends on what China is going to do in the next one two months," one trader said.
July paper was last quoted at $23.25/$23.45 down from Wednesday's $23.45/$23.55 with August pegged at $23.45/$23.55 down 15 cents, brokers said.
The weaker prices were attributed to the 15 cents loss to overnight crude values where July Brent closed at $17.35 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange.
Traders said the market is expected to drift with crude over the next few days in the absence of fresh indicators.
"Unless there is fresh buying support on the physical spot market, prices are not likely to increase," one trader said.
A group of traders who had since March 3 bought over 22 million barrels of gas oil are no longer giving the market the same kind of support.
Their withdrawal from the market on Monday against a background of a slump in crude prices led to a sharp drop in gas oil prices.
Traders said the market will only pick up if China comes back to buy in a big way July barrels to clear up the current physical overhang.
Physical gas oil on Wednesday rebounded slightly to above $23.00 per barrel after trading at $22.90 on Tuesday, with no deals concluded.
Fuel oil swaps were steady despite the fall in crude with July was indicated at $98.50/$99.50.
